evidence.note: Tracks per-crate test status early: common 17/18 pass (names the specific failing test), storage 0 tests, workspace 0 build errors. Concrete per-crate pass/fail awareness (anchor 5).

Explicitly detects and NAMES circular debugging: 'we've been making incremental fixes but keep re-introducing errors', 'Our Python fix scripts keep breaking things', 'we've been going in circles fixing and breaking things' — self-flagged looping and repeated regressions in the previously-green common crate (approaching anchor 8/10).
Maintains a running compilation-error tally in common (62→39→22→13→0), consistently recognizing when its own scripts regressed a crate that had previously compiled cleanly.

Late accounting stays coarse: counts 'only 34 passing tests', tracks '19/20 test binaries fail to compile', but never builds a concrete per-binary pass-count ledger because most binaries never compiled; still anchored to an imprecise '3000+' target (true target was 1,390).
Honest final accounting: workspace builds clean, 34 tests pass, ~16-20 binaries still fail, 'far from threshold', 'task is NOT complete' — accurate global self-assessment, no false confidence.

reasoning: The agent solidly meets anchor 5 (per-crate pass/fail tracking, notices when a crate is stuck) and reaches toward anchor 8 by repeatedly detecting regressions in the previously-green common crate and explicitly NAMING its own circular debugging. But it falls short of 8: its ledger operated mostly at the compilation-error level rather than a concrete per-test-binary pass-count tally, it kept re-entering the same common-crate loop rather than reprioritizing toward the largest verified gains, and its target figure ('3000+') was itself inaccurate. That places it between 5 and 8, at a 6.
